purpose: Implement the existing EG-CORRECT, EG-FAULT, and EG-INTEGRITY registry runners for the active xtask tooling scope without changing product behavior or Qualification Cell state.

change.public_seam: cargo xtask quality returned verdict and retained target/quality/evidence attempt

dependency_review.necessity: Rust std does not expose safe descriptor-relative create, open, link, rename, unlink, or directory enumeration APIs on all four registered macOS and Linux hosts. rustix is scoped only to xtask and supplies the safe I/O-owned wrappers needed to close validation/use races without a Positron unsafe boundary.

direct.security: The boundary uses rustix OwnedFd and safe openat, mkdirat, linkat, renameat, unlinkat, statat, and Dir APIs with O_NOFOLLOW and exact resource bounds. cargo audit reported no vulnerability for the 47-package lock graph; cargo deny accepted advisories, licenses, sources, and exact rustix 1.1.4 bans; Cargo Vet accepted the exact safe-to-deploy entry.
direct.maintenance: Bytecode Alliance maintains rustix with a published security-reporting process. Exact 1.1.4 is the current reviewed release, declares rust-version 1.63, and documents the required safe fs APIs for the registered Apple and Linux targets.
direct.removal: Remove when Rust std provides portable safe descriptor-relative filesystem operations on every registered host.

dependency_review.resolution: Cargo.lock intentionally adds only rustix 1.1.4 and the five exact transitives above. No prior dependency or exemption version changed, and no existing exemption criterion was broadened.

runner_changes: The active xtask tooling scope participates in risk-gate selection only through its own registered risk_gates set; no application, artifact, or deferred gate is inferred.

One immutable execution context captures bounded adversarial-manifest, quality-registry, integrity-registry, and fixture-harness bytes once; it parses the typed registries once and derives fixture, seed, and schedule identity from those exact bytes. Evidence identity and all three runners receive that same context and never reread the registered inputs.

EG-CORRECT launches the explicitly registered current-xtask Quality Engineering writer process with a cleared environment, waits within the registered deadline for an atomically published exact PID and publication-point acknowledgement, force-kills and reaps the writer, launches a distinct recovery process, and accepts only its externally readable predecessor-or-successor state and recovery digest.

EG-FAULT maps nine typed publication points one-to-one to the required partial-write, crash, restart, corruption, full-disk, clock, cancellation, network, and provider schedules. Every writer is force-killed and reaped at its acknowledged point and every verdict comes from a fresh recovery process over durable state.

EG-INTEGRITY persists identity-bound fixture objects, reopens the golden object, corrupts and deletes attempt-owned copies, requires digest-mismatch and missing-object failures, and proves the untouched prior object remains readable after each adversarial case.

Each gate claims one must-create no-follow fixture root directly beneath the canonical attempt TMPDIR, then performs every fixture create, read, write, copy, link, rename, removal, and recursive cleanup relative to held directory descriptors. Writer and recovery children verify exact device/inode identity tokens before mutation; occupied, symbolic-link, non-directory, escaped, swapped, and identity-changed paths fail closed.

An RAII owner reconciles the exact attempt-owned gate tree on success, detector failure, forced writer termination, recovery failure, and timeout; it synchronizes the attempt parent after removal, converts cleanup failure into a failed gate, and retains only immutable process observations and recovery digests in raw evidence.

All frozen fixture inputs and process records are opened no-follow through their held parent descriptors, checked against their byte ceiling before allocation, read through a maximum-plus-one stream bound into a pre-reserved buffer, and rejected if their opened identity or metadata drifts during the read.

The internal quality-fixture child interface accepts only its exact registered writer or recovery arity, including parent-claimed directory identities, and rejects any trailing argument before dispatch.

EG-TEST retains its exact locked workspace, all-targets, all-features, no-retry CI selection and the existing 131072-byte per-stream ceiling. Its Nextest invocation overrides only live and final status verbosity to failure level, preserves immediate-final failure output from the registered CI profile, requires exactly one terminal canonical summary, rejects missing or ambiguous counts and any skipped test, and retains the completed-test count in the gate detail.
unchanged: All 25 gate IDs, stages, coordinators, timeouts, memory declarations, exception classes, targets, thresholds, and application activation ledgers.
The EG-TEST suite selection, failure exit semantics, failure output, retry policy, timeout policy, and controlled stream ceiling.
Developer evidence remains diagnostic and non-merge-eligible.
Release Qualification Cells remain Specified; an engineering runner implementation does not qualify a product artifact.

detection_gained: An active xtask scope can no longer select EG-CORRECT, EG-FAULT, or EG-INTEGRITY and receive an unsupported-runner failure instead of a retained fixture result.

A false predecessor-or-successor oracle, a malformed or oversized fixture registry, and a missing publication-point schedule fail closed through the public quality seam and retain a failed named-gate outcome.
Corrupt fixture bytes are classified as a digest mismatch, deleted fixture objects are classified as missing, and neither adversarial case can mutate or replace its prior persisted object.

The retained report records exact fixture IDs, seeds, fault schedules, writer and recovery process identities, forced termination and reap, externally observed states, recovery digests, identity-field coverage, and the frozen fixture-registry binding rather than a synthesized cargo self-test verdict.

Mutation after fixture capture cannot alter execution or evidence, a symlink claim race cannot write outside the attempt root, repeated runs do not accumulate fixture trees, timed-out writers are killed and reaped, and cleanup failure fails the named gate.

The expanded first-class regression inventory cannot exhaust EG-TEST evidence capture through successful per-test status repetition; failures remain visible, and successful evidence carries the exact completed-test count with zero skips.
The active tooling selection regression test proves EG-CONCURRENCY, EG-CRYPTO, EG-RESOURCE, and EG-SOAK remain explicitly not selected when xtask selects only its registered gates.

lifecycle_test_map.pass: The three quality_runs_*_through_the_registered_public_seam fixtures execute the durable detectors and inspect named-gate evidence and immutable raw reports; the correctness and fault reports prove acknowledged writer termination plus fresh-process recovery.
lifecycle_test_map.fail: The false correctness oracle, missing fault schedule, false integrity reopen outcome, symlink race, and injected cleanup failure fixtures each return a failed named-gate outcome through cargo xtask quality.
lifecycle_test_map.timeout_and_cancellation: quality_kills_reaps_and_cleans_a_timed_out_fixture_writer proves a writer that omits its registered acknowledgement is forcibly terminated, reaped, and cleaned before the deadline failure is retained. The parent launches no shell and each child uses the fixed current xtask executable with a cleared environment and no descendants.
lifecycle_test_map.missing_tool: The M0-06 environment snapshot and controlled launch-failure tests fail the attempt before an unavailable external detector can run. EG-CORRECT, EG-FAULT, and EG-INTEGRITY themselves use only owned Rust and filesystem operations and make no missing-tool claim.
lifecycle_test_map.malformed: quality_rejects_a_malformed_correctness_fixture_registry and the existing malformed retained-evidence/raw-report tests reject malformed detector inputs and durable outputs.
lifecycle_test_map.stale: quality_rejects_stale_trusted_ci_source_identity and the existing registered command, environment, registry, report-digest, and result cross-reference checks remain gate-generic and cover attempts containing these named gates.
lifecycle_test_map.retry: quality_preserves_a_failed_correctness_attempt_before_a_later_pass proves a later successful detector run cannot erase or rewrite the prior failed attempt; the existing trusted-CI retry rejection remains unchanged.
lifecycle_test_map.resource_ceiling: quality_rejects_a_correctness_fixture_registry_over_its_resource_ceiling proves the 16384-byte detector registry ceiling; the registered process protocol bounds wait time and record size; existing M0-06 raw-report step, stream, report, path, environment, and retained-attempt ceilings remain shared.
lifecycle_test_map.cleanup: Repeated successful attempts, false-oracle failure, every normally force-killed writer, an injected writer timeout, and an injected cleanup failure cover cleanup success and failure. Mutable fixture paths are absent from retained reports, and the attempt parent is synchronized after successful removal.

old.result: Before the change, an active registered EG-FAULT selection failed with an unsupported runner outcome.

new.result: The named process-backed state-transition, nine-class one-to-one fault schedule, frozen-input, no-follow ownership, bounded cleanup, identity-bound corruption/deletion, and bounded full-selection EG-TEST command-contract fixtures passed through their registry-selected public seams locally. These local results are diagnostic only.

compatibility_and_recovery.compatibility: The cargo xtask quality command and evidence schema remain unchanged. The quality-fixture command is an internal registered Quality Engineering child-process interface invoked only by cargo xtask quality. Correctness, fault, and integrity reports use the existing immutable selected-gate raw-report contract; exact seed and fault-schedule identity bindings are populated only when these fixture gates are selected.
compatibility_and_recovery.recovery: Correct the failing registered fixture, instrumentation mapping, or persisted-object behavior and create a new quality attempt. Retain every failed attempt and its raw report; do not overwrite or reclassify earlier evidence.
